mcq.q: Which action shows attentive listening?
options: Looking at the speaker and staying quiet
mcq.explanation: Attentive listening means giving your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker.

mcq.q: What is the difference between hearing and listening?
options: Hearing needs effort but listening does not
Listening is done on purpose and hearing happens by itself
mcq.explanation: Hearing happens naturally, but listening is a choice to pay attention.

mcq.q: A noun is a word that
options: names a person, animal, place or thing
mcq.explanation: Nouns are naming words.

mcq.q: Which of these words is a noun?
mcq.explanation: Millet is a grain, so it names a thing. The others are an action, a describing word and an adverb.

mcq.q: Singular means
mcq.explanation: A singular noun names one person, animal, place or thing.

mcq.q: Plural means
mcq.explanation: Plural nouns name two or more.

mcq.q: What is the plural of the English word cup?
mcq.explanation: Most English nouns add s to make the plural.

mcq.q: What is the plural of the English word mango?
mcq.explanation: Mango takes es in the plural, mangoes.

mcq.q: What is the plural of the English word loaf?
mcq.explanation: Loaf changes f to ves in the plural.

mcq.q: How should you find out how your mother tongue forms plurals?
options: Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
mcq.explanation: Languages form plurals in different ways, so we ask people who know the language well.

mcq.q: In a singing game, who gives the instructions?
mcq.explanation: The soloist leads by singing the instructions and the group responds.

mcq.q: What should you do before acting on a spoken instruction?
mcq.explanation: Listening to the end helps you act correctly.

mcq.q: Why do we keep a class portfolio of songs?
options: So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten
mcq.explanation: A portfolio preserves the songs collected from the community.

mcq.q: What is polite when you collect a song from an elder?
options: Greet them and thank them at the end
mcq.explanation: Good manners include greeting, listening and thanking.

mcq.q: Which sentence contains only singular nouns?
mcq.explanation: Girl and basket each name one thing.

mcq.q: Which is the key question of this lesson?
options: How should we respond to instructions?
What is the price of food?
mcq.explanation: The lesson asks how we should respond to instructions in songs and games.

mcq.q: What does reading for information mean?
mcq.explanation: We read for information to find facts and learn.

mcq.q: Vocabulary means
options: all the words you know and can use
mcq.explanation: Vocabulary is a person's collection of words.

mcq.q: What is a good first step when reading for information?
options: Ask what you want to find out
mcq.explanation: A question in mind helps you look for the right facts.

mcq.q: How can flashcards help with vocabulary?
options: They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
mcq.explanation: Flashcards are a simple tool for revision.

mcq.q: A word bank is
options: a class list of useful words on one theme
mcq.explanation: A vocabulary bank collects words by topic.

mcq.q: Which sentence has a plural noun?
mcq.explanation: Bananas is plural, and the number three shows there are more than one.

mcq.q: Which word in this sentence is singular: The seller has an onion and two cabbages?
mcq.explanation: Onion names one thing. Cabbages is plural.

mcq.q: What does fluent reading mean?
options: Reading very slowly word by word
Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
mcq.explanation: Fluent readers read smoothly.

mcq.q: What is a good way to give feedback to a reader?
options: Say one good thing and one thing to improve
mcq.explanation: Kind and useful feedback helps people improve.

mcq.q: Where should you look to check an answer to a comprehension question?
mcq.explanation: Good readers go back to the text.

mcq.q: Which is a clue that a noun is plural?
options: A number word such as three before it
mcq.explanation: Number words show how many there are.

mcq.q: In the passage: Ugali is made from maize flour, what is ugali made from?
mcq.explanation: The passage states that ugali is made from maize flour.

mcq.q: Reading a text once for the general meaning is done
mcq.explanation: A first reading gives the main idea.

mcq.q: Why should you underline new words in a text?
options: So you can find their meanings and learn them
mcq.explanation: Underlining marks the words to study.

mcq.q: Which of these is a cultural food word?
mcq.explanation: Porridge is a food. The others are not.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT a way of building vocabulary?
mcq.explanation: Ignoring new words does not build vocabulary.

mcq.q: What does legible writing mean?
options: Writing that can be read easily
mcq.explanation: Legible means easy to read.

mcq.q: Why is neat handwriting important?
options: It makes the pencil last longer
It helps the reader to understand the message
mcq.explanation: A message is useful only if it can be read.

mcq.q: Where should letters sit in a lined book?
mcq.explanation: Letters rest on the base line.

mcq.q: What should you leave between two words?
mcq.explanation: A finger width keeps words clear.

mcq.q: Which is a good way to practise the shape of a letter?
options: Trace it in the air with your finger
mcq.explanation: Tracing helps the hand remember the movement.

mcq.q: A sentence should begin with
mcq.explanation: Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

mcq.q: A sentence should end with a
mcq.explanation: A statement ends with a full stop.

mcq.q: How should you sit when you write?
options: Straight, with your book in front of you
mcq.explanation: Good posture helps neat writing.

mcq.q: What should you do if you make a mistake in your exercise book?
options: Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
mcq.explanation: Neat correction keeps the page clean.

mcq.q: Tall letters such as b and d usually reach
mcq.explanation: Tall letters go up to the top line.

mcq.q: Which letter hangs below the base line in English handwriting?
mcq.explanation: The letter g has a tail that goes below the line.

mcq.q: What is a gallery walk in handwriting practice?
options: Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display
mcq.explanation: Pupils view and comment on displayed work.

mcq.q: A good comment during a gallery walk is
mcq.explanation: Kind and specific comments help writers.

mcq.q: When copying a sentence, what should you check?
options: Only the colour of the pen
Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
mcq.explanation: These are the points of neat copying.

mcq.q: Which pencil grip is best?
options: Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger
Hold it by the end with your teeth
mcq.explanation: A light grip prevents tiredness.

mcq.q: Why should you not rush the last lines of a page?
options: Neatness can be lost when you hurry
mcq.explanation: Careful writing should stay the same to the end.

mcq.q: What is an instruction?
options: Words that tell someone what to do
mcq.explanation: An instruction says what to do.

mcq.q: Which of these is an instruction?
mcq.explanation: Close the door tells you what to do.

mcq.q: A verb is
options: a word that names a person
a word that describes a colour
a word that shows an action
mcq.explanation: Verbs show what is done.

mcq.q: Which word in Bring the clothes inside is the verb?
mcq.explanation: Bring shows the action.

mcq.q: Which words show the order of steps?
mcq.explanation: Sequence words show the order.

mcq.q: Which game teaches that messages can change when passed on?
mcq.explanation: In Chinese whisper the message changes as it passes.

mcq.q: In Simon says, when should you obey an instruction?
options: Only when it begins with Simon says
mcq.explanation: The game is about listening carefully.

mcq.q: Why should instructions be clear?
options: So the listener can do the right thing
mcq.explanation: Clear instructions prevent mistakes.

mcq.q: Which instruction is clearer?
options: Put the bucket under the roof to collect rain water.
mcq.explanation: It says what, where and why.

mcq.q: What should you do first when you give an instruction to a friend?
options: Say all steps at once quickly
mcq.explanation: Planning helps to give clear instructions.

mcq.q: What does an oral text mean?
options: A text written on a wall
mcq.explanation: Oral means spoken.

mcq.q: Which sentence gives information but not an instruction?
mcq.explanation: It only tells about the weather.

mcq.q: What can a weather forecast tell us?
options: What the weather will be like
mcq.explanation: A forecast predicts the weather.

mcq.q: What is a good response when you did not understand an instruction?
options: Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
mcq.explanation: Polite questions help you understand.

mcq.q: Which sentence uses a signal word for the last step?
options: Finally, wait until the rain stops.
mcq.explanation: Finally shows the last step.

mcq.q: What is intonation?
options: The rise and fall of the voice
mcq.explanation: Intonation is voice movement.

mcq.q: In English, what usually happens to the voice at the end of a question?
options: It stays exactly the same always
mcq.explanation: Many questions end with a rising voice.

mcq.q: What does reading with expression mean?
options: Showing feeling in your voice as you read
mcq.explanation: Expression shows the feelings in the text.

mcq.q: What should a reader do at a full stop?
mcq.explanation: Full stops tell us to pause.

mcq.q: Fluent reading needs
options: smooth pace, correct words and good expression
mcq.explanation: These are the parts of fluency.

mcq.q: Which way of reading a sad part is best?
mcq.explanation: A slow, soft voice matches sadness.

mcq.q: What is reader's theatre?
options: Reading a script aloud with different parts
mcq.explanation: Pupils read parts with expression.

mcq.q: A newsreader on the radio should speak
options: clearly and at a steady pace
mcq.explanation: News should be clear and easy to follow.

mcq.q: What does a comma tell a reader?
mcq.explanation: Commas show short pauses.

mcq.q: Which sentence should be read with a rising voice in English?
mcq.explanation: It is a question.

mcq.q: Why is reading fluently important?
options: It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
mcq.explanation: Fluent reading helps meaning.

mcq.q: Which is a mistake in reading aloud?
options: Reading too fast so nobody can follow
mcq.explanation: Speed that is too fast loses meaning.

mcq.q: What should listeners do after a group reads aloud?
mcq.explanation: Feedback helps readers improve.

mcq.q: How can recording your reading help you?
options: You can listen back and see how to improve
mcq.explanation: Playing back shows where to improve.

mcq.q: Which feeling could a strong, fast voice show?
mcq.explanation: Excitement is often read faster and stronger.

short.q: Explain what attentive listening means.
short.answer: Attentive listening means choosing to give your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker so that you understand and remember what is said.
short.working: One mark for choosing to pay attention and one mark for understanding or remembering.

short.q: Write the plural of each English noun: plate, tomato.
short.answer: plates, tomatoes
short.working: One mark for each correct plural.

short.q: List three habits of an attentive listener.
short.answer: Face the speaker, stay quiet, think about the words, wait for your turn, respond correctly (any three).
short.working: One mark for each habit, up to three.

short.q: Pick out the nouns in this song line: We roast the maize and boil the beans.
short.answer: maize and beans (and we is a pronoun, not a noun)
short.working: One mark for maize, one mark for beans, and one mark for not including roast or boil, which are actions.

short.q: Describe how a class can collect and keep cultural songs from the community.
short.answer: Ask elders politely, listen carefully, write or record the song with permission, note the name of the person who shared it and the date, and store it in a class portfolio.
short.working: One mark for each of four correct steps.

short.q: Play the role of the soloist in a singing game. Write three short instructions you would sing and say what the group should do for each.
short.answer: Any three clear instructions with matching actions, for example Clap two times (the group claps twice), Stir the pot (the group pretends to stir), Turn around (the group turns).
short.working: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for each matching response, with a total of five marks for three well matched pairs and correct listening steps.

short.q: What is a vocabulary bank and why is it useful?
short.answer: It is a class list of words on one theme. It helps pupils remember and use new words.
short.working: One mark for the meaning and one for the use.

short.q: Give the plural of each English noun: cabbage, onion.
short.answer: cabbages, onions
short.working: One mark for each correct plural.

short.q: Read: Millet porridge is a warm drink made by mixing millet flour with water and boiling it. What is it made from and how is it cooked?
short.answer: It is made from millet flour and water and it is cooked by boiling.
short.working: One mark for millet flour, one for water, one for boiling.

short.q: State three steps for building vocabulary from a text.
short.answer: Read once for meaning, underline new words, write them on flashcards with meanings, use each in a sentence (any three).
short.working: One mark for each step.

short.q: Describe how a group can read a text aloud together and give feedback.
short.answer: Read silently first, help each other with hard words, take turns to read, then listen to the group and give one good point and one point to improve in a kind way.
short.working: One mark for each of four correct parts.

short.q: Read: Mama Wanjiru buys tomatoes, an onion and three cabbages at the market. List the nouns and say which are singular and which are plural.
short.answer: Nouns: Mama Wanjiru, tomatoes, onion, cabbages, market. Singular: Mama Wanjiru, onion, market. Plural: tomatoes, cabbages.
short.working: One mark for finding all five nouns, two marks for correct singular nouns and two marks for correct plural nouns.

short.q: Give two reasons why neat handwriting matters.
short.answer: It helps the reader to understand the message, and it shows respect and builds confidence.
short.working: One mark for each sensible reason.

short.q: Copy this sentence correctly: the food is hot
short.answer: The food is hot.
short.working: One mark for the capital letter and one mark for the full stop.

short.q: Describe three rules for writing tidily on lined paper.
short.answer: Letters sit on the base line, tall letters reach the top line, keep a finger space between words, and start on the left.
short.working: One mark for each rule, up to three.

short.q: Name three ways to practise letter shapes before writing them.
short.answer: Trace in the air, trace on a card, model with clay or string, paint them.
short.working: One mark for each way.

short.q: Explain how to take part in a class handwriting gallery walk.
short.answer: Write your best sentence on a strip. Display it on the wall. Walk quietly, look at each strip, and leave a kind and helpful comment.
short.working: One mark for each of four points.

short.q: Write a short paragraph of three sentences about why we should write neatly. Check your capital letters and full stops.
short.answer: Any three neat, complete sentences, for example Neat writing helps others to read my work. It shows respect for the reader. I feel proud when my book is tidy.
short.working: One mark for each correct sentence, one mark for capital letters and one for full stops.

short.q: What is a verb? Give two examples.
short.answer: A verb is an action word. Examples: run, close, bring, put.
short.working: One mark for the meaning and one mark for two correct examples.

short.q: Write the verbs in this instruction: Close the door and sit down.
short.answer: close, sit
short.working: One mark for each verb.

short.q: Give three signal words used to show the order of steps.
short.answer: first, next, then, after that, finally (any three).
short.working: One mark for each.

short.q: Explain why clear instructions are important when it rains.
short.answer: Clear instructions tell people what to do to stay safe and dry, so they do not make mistakes or get hurt.
short.working: One mark for staying safe, one for avoiding mistakes, one for a clear link to rain.

short.q: Write three instructions for what to do when it starts to rain at school. Use first, then and finally.
short.answer: First, go into the classroom. Then close the windows. Finally, wait for the rain to stop.
short.working: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for using all three signal words.

short.q: Describe how you would play Simon says with your class and say what it teaches.
short.answer: One pupil is the leader. The leader gives instructions. Pupils obey only when the leader says Simon says. Those who obey a wrong instruction are out. The game teaches careful listening.
short.working: One mark for the leader, one for the rule, one for what happens when a player breaks the rule, and two marks for explaining what it teaches.

short.q: What is intonation?
short.answer: The rise and fall of the voice as we speak.
short.working: One mark for rise and one for fall of the voice.

short.q: Give two reasons why we read fluently.
short.answer: It helps listeners understand and enjoy, and it helps the reader to understand the text.
short.working: One mark for each reason.

short.q: List three ways of reading with expression.
short.answer: Change loudness, change speed, pause at punctuation, use different voices for characters, use face and hands.
short.working: One mark for each way.

short.q: Explain how the meaning of You are coming to school changes when it is a statement and when it is a question.
short.answer: As a statement the voice falls and it tells something. As a question the voice rises and it asks something.
short.working: One mark for each of the two meanings and one mark for the voice movement.

short.q: Describe how a newsreader should read a weather bulletin.
short.answer: Speak clearly, keep a steady pace, use a friendly and confident tone, pause at full stops and look at the audience.
short.working: One mark for each of four correct points.

short.q: Plan a reader's theatre for a short passage about rain. Say who the roles are, how to practise and how the audience gives feedback.
short.answer: Roles such as narrator, farmer, child and rain. Read your part silently three times, mark stressed words, then read aloud with expression. The audience gives one good point and one improvement.
short.working: Two marks for suitable roles, two marks for practice steps and one mark for feedback.
